sources.title: AI overview
sources.finding: Zed separates its native agent, external ACP agents and terminal threads, with several threads running across projects.

sources.title: LLM providers
sources.finding: Native Zed AI has hosted, API, subscription, gateway and local model setup routes; these settings do not configure external agents.

sources.title: Agent panel
sources.finding: Independent threads have history and optional worktrees. Steer works for Zed Agent, while external-agent history and token support vary.

sources.title: Remote development
sources.finding: Local UI and model communication remain local while source files, language servers, tasks and terminals run on an SSH server.

sources.title: Collaboration
sources.finding: Signed-in users can simultaneously edit a shared project and use channels and voice; project sharing exposes its local filesystem.

sources.title: Sandboxing
sources.finding: OS sandboxing covers Zed Agent terminal/fetch tools, not external agents or terminal threads; platform-specific limits apply.

sources.title: Tool permissions
sources.finding: Tool rules support allow, deny and confirm; deny takes precedence and built-in security rules cannot be overridden.

sources.title: AI privacy
sources.locator: AI request paths; retention and training
sources.finding: Zed describes no default retention of prompts/code and separates hosted commitments from own-provider terms; some models have safety-retention exceptions.

sources.title: Telemetry in Zed
sources.finding: Client metrics and diagnostics can be disabled; hosted AI/collaboration metadata remains necessary for those services.

sources.title: Plans & pricing
sources.finding: The editor works without an account. Pro includes $5 monthly usage, metered at provider list price plus 10%, with configurable spend limits.

sources.title: Git
sources.finding: Zed displays working tree, staging and branch state with native Git controls; unsupported operations can use the terminal.

sources.title: Zed pinned README
sources.finding: This pinned README states primarily GPL-3.0-or-later with Apache-2.0 components where marked; hosted-service parity does not follow.

sources.title: Zed roadmap
sources.locator: Currently working on; Coming up next
sources.finding: The roadmap lists async collaboration in progress and Web and Plan Mode next; undated plans are not current capabilities.

sources.title: CLI Reference
sources.finding: Product-owned zed CLI opens files/directories, remote projects and diff views; wait/reuse/add options integrate with other tools. This is an editor launcher, not a headless agent API.

sources.title: External Agents
sources.locator: Registry; Common agents; Configuration; Custom agents
sources.finding: Zed ACP registry supports Claude, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi among others. Custom ACP command/args/env adapters are configurable. External auth/tools/retention remain agent owned.

sources.title: Parallel Agents
sources.finding: Threads run independently with different native/external agents, own history and context. History archives/restores/deletes, agent-dependent imports and detached-HEAD worktree save/restore are documented.

sources.title: Agent Panel
sources.finding: Panel supports queued/steer messages, native thread history and summaries, per-hunk keep/reject, multi-buffer review, context attachments and token counts. External integration feature parity varies.

sources.title: Tools
sources.finding: Native tools include grep/find/read, diagnostics, fetch/search_web, file edits, terminal and spawn_agent with a separate context window. Pro/Zed-provider-only web search is distinct from MCP search.

sources.title: Agent Settings
sources.finding: Subagents inherit model/effort/speed by default or use agent.subagent_model. Requested models preserve configured controls with documented fallback; compaction defaults to ninety percent context.

sources.title: MCP
sources.finding: Zed connects local/remote MCP servers through configuration/extensions with headers or OAuth. Native profiles and per-tool permission rules apply; ACP forwarding and external native config are separate.

sources.title: Instructions
sources.finding: Personal AGENTS.md and compatible project instruction files provide persistent context; project rules override personal instructions. External/terminal agents have their own loaders.

sources.title: Skills
sources.finding: SKILL.md packages are created/imported, scoped global/project, editable/deletable and shared as self-contained links requiring explicit recipient save. Model-loaded skills follow tool permissions; manual invocation is explicit.

sources.title: Agent Profiles
sources.finding: Write enables edits/commands, Ask is read-only and Minimal has no project tools. Profiles set tool availability and default model; permission rules are separate and external agents do not inherit these profiles.

sources.title: Tool Permissions
sources.finding: Native tools support allow/deny/confirm patterns. Hardcoded protections and always_deny outrank auto-approve; chained shell commands are individually checked. ACP/terminal-agent boundaries remain separate.

sources.title: Dev Containers
sources.finding: Zed builds/opens devcontainers with Docker or Podman and runs tasks, terminals and language servers there. Config changes do not rebuild automatically; users restart and reopen.

sources.title: Roles
sources.finding: Business organizations use Owner, Admin, Billing Manager and Member with explicit administration/feature/billing rights. Removing membership revokes org-managed access without disabling personal editor use.

sources.title: Channels
sources.finding: Channels offer real-time shared code editing, voice and Markdown notes. Guests are read-only unless temporarily granted write access. Unsharing disconnects collaborators; terminal following is not supported.

sources.title: Use a Local Model
sources.finding: Native Zed features work with local llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio or an OpenAI-compatible server using configured model/base URL. Endpoint auth is customer controlled.

sources.title: Authenticate with Zed
sources.finding: Editor use needs no login. Own-key AI can work without Zed sign-in; hosted models and real-time collaboration require Zed’s GitHub OAuth account.

sources.title: AI Privacy
sources.finding: Zed normally retains no prompt/code context; provider contracts prohibit training but designated safety-retention models are exceptions to ZDR. Feedback/training sharing is explicit opt-in. BYOK/external/terminal paths follow their own providers.

sources.title: Telemetry in Zed
sources.finding: Client metrics/crashes can be disabled independently. Hosted-service metadata needed for billing/rate limiting remains required; account-linked random IDs and inspectable logs are documented.

sources.title: Plans & Pricing
sources.finding: Free editor includes own-key and external-agent use. Pro is ten dollars monthly with five token dollars; hosted usage is provider list plus ten percent. Trial is fourteen days/no card and shares balance with Delta; no Delta execution capability is inferred.

sources.title: Developing Zed
sources.finding: Vendor developer documentation identifies Rust crates, GPU-accelerated GPUI, native editor/project/workspace components and a separate collaboration server.

sources.title: Use an Existing Subscription
sources.finding: ChatGPT Plus/Pro authenticates as a native Zed provider without API key; Claude Pro/Max uses external Claude or CLI. OpenCode uses API keys; Cursor uses its external/CLI route.

sources.title: Zed Agent sandboxing
sources.finding: Native sandbox blocks terminal networking and out-of-scope writes by default when enabled. macOS uses Seatbelt, Linux Bubblewrap and Windows WSL Bubblewrap only. Non-terminal fetch does not inherit terminal network limits.

sources.locator: TaskId and SpawnInTerminal; crates/agent/src/db.rs and thread_store.rs; bounded agent/agent_ui/task source searches for issue, backlog and ticket
sources.finding: Editor tasks are shell commands spawned in terminal tabs. Agent history stores conversation threads, not independent issue/backlog records. A bounded source inspection of task, agent and agent_ui found no native issue entity or issue state machine; GitHub issue operations through MCP remain external.

sources.title: Zed crates/agent/src/agent.rs
sources.locator: NativeAgent session/prompt handling; crates/agent_ui actions; crates/task/src/task_template.rs; bounded cron/scheduler/webhook search
sources.finding: Agent work starts through editor/session prompt actions. The inspected agent and agent_ui modules have no scheduler or webhook-to-agent run service. Editor TaskHook only has CreateWorktree and runs shell setup, not scheduled autonomous agent work.

sources.title: Zed ACP Registry installation and agent threads
sources.locator: Install from the ACP Registry; Start an External Agent Thread
sources.finding: Zed installs registry agents through zed: acp registry or Agent Settings/Add Agent. Installed agents appear in the Agent Panel and Threads Sidebar new-thread menu. Zed manages their threads while each ACP agent owns its runtime and authentication; the common-agent list is explicitly not exhaustive.
